data.one_liner: A Flutter widget that lets you swipe through a deck of cards with gestures or buttons.
data.what_it_does: SwipingCardDeck renders a stack of cards and allows the user to swipe left or right, triggering callbacks. It supports custom card widgets, swipe thresholds, animation duration, and optional drag disabling.
use_when: You need a Tinder‑style card stack for decision making or matching apps
You want a lightweight, customizable swipe widget without external dependencies
avoid_when: You need vertical swiping or complex gesture handling beyond left/right
You require integration with state‑management libraries that expect a different API
strengths: Easy to integrate, no extra dependencies
Optimized to render only the top two cards for performance
Fully customizable callbacks and swipe parameters
Supports both gesture and button‑based swiping
weaknesses: No built‑in state management or persistence
data.minimal_example:
SwipingCardDeck(
  cardDeck: [
    Card(color: Colors.red, child: SizedBox(height: 300, width: 200)),
    Card(color: Colors.green, child: SizedBox(height: 300, width: 200)),
  ],
  onDeckEmpty: () => debugPrint("Card deck empty"),
  onLeftSwipe: (card) => debugPrint("Swiped left!"),
  onRightSwipe: (card) => debugPrint("Swiped right!"),
  swipeThreshold: MediaQuery.of(context).size.width / 4,
  minimumVelocity: 1000,
  cardWidth: 200,
  rotationFactor: 0.8 / 3.14,
  swipeAnimationDuration: const Duration(milliseconds: 500),
  disableDragging: false,
);
